page: Amazon Web Services r8i-flex.16xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor running at 3.9 GHz. The configuration includes 64 dedicated vCPUs across 32 physical cores, supporting hyper-threading with 2.0 threads per core. Memory capacity is 512.0 GB of DDR5 RAM operating at 7 GHz, yielding 8.0 GB of memory per core. The processor is equipped with a 480 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache.

The CPU architecture supports advanced instruction sets, including Intel Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX, AVX512), Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX tile and int8), and cryptographic acceleration via AES, VAES, and SHA_NI. In benchmark testing, the instance demonstrates strong multi-core capabilities, scoring in the top 25% for stress-ng multi-core, PassMark CPU, and Geekbench multi-core tests. Single-core performance is more varied, with stress-ng single-core scoring in the average tier, while Geekbench single-core and text processing reach the top 10% tier.

The system utilizes high-speed DDR5 memory, achieving top 25% performance in read-only memory bandwidth for both small and large blocks, though large block write bandwidth remains in the average tier. There is no local NVMe storage bundled with this instance, meaning all storage requirements must be met via network-attached options over the baseline 15 Gbps network interface.

This hardware profile is optimized for workloads requiring high memory density and parallel processing without the need for local physical disks. It achieves top 10% performance in static web serving throughput, software compilation, and prompt processing for small language models. The inclusion of AMX instructions supports efficient low-precision matrix operations, making it suitable for CPU-based LLM inference, where it maintains strong performance on medium-sized models.
